commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

# Spec: werk v0

## Problem Statement

A person who builds software with Claude Code works in a chat transcript. The transcript only grows. The decisions that the conversation settles are buried in it, and nobody can see which decision rests on which other decision. When one decision changes, nothing marks the decisions that depend on it.

The person also cannot see the build. An agent that builds from the decisions works in a terminal. The person does not see which slice of work is running, which one failed, or why. To run two topics at once, the person opens a second terminal, and the second conversation starts empty and pays again for the context that the first one already holds.

werk has a working prototype of the answer. Its code was written to find the right shape, not to keep. It has shortcuts and it is difficult to change. The person needs a clean v0 that is built only from the decided cards, so that the cards prove they are enough to rebuild the behaviour (#werk-base).

## Solution

werk v0 is a visual layer over Claude Code with three views: the map, the board, and the chat (#werk).

1. **The map** draws the fold of an append-only log of decisions (#pr-log, #werk-write). Each card has a reason, typed links, options, and sources. 3. **The board** shows the tickets of a build run in five columns. The person starts the run, triggers or stops one ticket, reorders, and archives (#werk-board).

Behind the board, the inner build loop turns a decided subtree into merged, tested code with no person in the middle (#werk-loop): a spec, then tickets, then a builder loop per ticket, then a merge loop per run, with an overseer that keeps every agent from getting stuck. v0 is a new project in its own repository. Bun runs the server TypeScript directly, Vite transforms a React client, and the server reloads its own modules without killing a live agent (#werk-stack, #werk-hmr, #werk-dev). The agent that builds werk has a test harness it can run itself (#werk-test).

## Implementation Decisions

### Project base

- v0 starts in a new, empty repository. Nothing is ported. The decided cards that #werk depends on are the spec. The prototype is a reference to read, not to copy (#werk-base).
- The kill criterion for the from-scratch choice is recorded on #werk. The prototype's behaviour sets the bar. If the criterion fires, the fallback is to extend the prototype code (#werk-base).
- Three parts: the log, the fold, and the web view (#werk). werk's log is its own working implementation of #pr-log, not a consumer of a separate engine.
- Bun runs the server TypeScript directly under `bun --hot` in dev (#werk-hmr). The client is React, transformed by Vite, so v0 has a client build step (#werk-stack). Islands are the hydration pattern, and progressive loading is a shape of the API, not a framework feature (#werk-stack).

### Modules

1. **Log.** An append-only file of events. Append and read only. No event is ever rewritten or deleted (#pr-log). A proposed card is its own event type, not a flag on an added card (#werk-propose-new).
2. **Fold.** A pure function from the event list to the map state: nodes with their latest words and status, live edges, held ghost edges, rollups, stale and paused marks with their trace, and the unchallenged count. A ghost sits in the nodes with a proposed flag and outside every derivation. Its edges wait in a separate set and go live when both ends are real (#werk-propose-new). Stale marks the next hop; paused marks every downstream card; stale wins over paused (#pr-wf-paused).
3. **Command line.** The only write path (#werk-write). Each verb appends events. It holds the contract check at the move to decided (#werk-contract), the accept gate for ghosts with its actor claim (#werk-propose-new), the find and remove verbs (#werk), the quote verb for excerpts (#werk-excerpt), the note verbs (#werk-chat), and the build verbs (#werk-loop). The command form of each verb lives on its own card under #werk-cli.
4. **Server.** One process per project directory, guarded by a lock with a 5-second wait and a port retry of 20 tries at 250 ms (#werk-dev). A guard on the global object keeps a hot reload from starting a second server or a second agent (#werk-hmr). It serves the client, the read API, and one live event channel (SSE). The channel pushes "changed" when the log changes and "reload" when the client code changes (#werk-dev). In dev, the server runs Vite inside its own process to transform the client. A client change that Vite cannot apply in place sends the "reload" event, and the composer draft is kept in session storage across it (#werk-client-reload).
5. **Conversation manager.** One Claude Code child per conversation, spoken to over stream-json (#werk-chat). It forks a session with the fork-session option (#werk-mc-fork), stores the session id and the home card of each conversation (#werk-mc-split), parks, un-parks, and reaps idle children after 30 minutes (#werk-mc-park), and keeps one ask at a time per conversation (#werk-mc-asks). It reports running, waiting, and dead per conversation (#werk-mc-live).
6. **Board state.** Ticket state is its own append-only log beside the decision log (#vi-board-state). The board view folds it into the five columns (#werk-board-columns). The board actions write to it through the server (#werk-board-control).
7. **Build pipeline.** Plan (spec, then tickets), builder loop, merge loop, held-out set, and overseer (#werk-loop). Each pass is a fresh headless agent in a worktree (#lp-stateless). Every time limit is a parameter (#st-build-seam). Every run writes a feature tier event first (#werk-loop-tier).
8. **Client.** Three views: the map, the board, and the chat pane (#werk). The Markdown renderer adds card links by the rules of #werk-reflink and boxes fenced code with highlighting (#werk-codeblock). The open card lives in the location hash. Each tab owns its card, its map position, and its draft (#werk-mc-follow).
9. **Fake agent.** One scripted binary that stands in for every Claude Code child: the chat agent, the builder, the grader, the reviewers, the classifiers, the step author, and the binder. It replays a scripted stream of events and edits files the way a real agent does (#st-build-seam, #werk-v0-seams).

### Interfaces between the modules

- The command line and the server both append through the log module. Neither writes a card in any other way (#werk-write).
- Every read goes through the fold. The browser, the command line, and the build pipeline read the same fold of the same log (#pr-log).
- The server talks to each agent over stream-json, as a child process (#werk-chat). The build pipeline starts a headless one-shot child per pass (#lp-stateless).
- The client gets the graph from the read API and refetches it on a "changed" event. It reloads itself on a "reload" event (#werk-dev).
- The board reads ticket state from its own log, not from card status (#vi-board-state).

### Contracts

- The chat request carries the text, the pasted images, the open card, and the active conversation tab. The reply streams over the live channel (#werk-chat).
- The server has a note route that appends a note and copies the `re #<id> "<title>": <text>` line to the clipboard. The browser never calls it (#werk-chat).
- An edge proposed with a card accepts or discards with that card, never alone. Accepting a child accepts its ghost refines ancestors. Discarding a card discards its ghost descendants. Accept is one card at a time (#werk-propose-new).
- A ticket has the fields title, what to build, acceptance criteria, stories, cites, blocked_by, and checks, and names no file paths (#st-ticket, #st-ticket-stories).
- The grader returns a score from 1 to 5, where 3 passes, and the gap for each card (#lp-prod-judge). A review finding has a severity, a file and a line, an impact, and a fix (#lp-prod-review).
- A builder pass appends one line to the run's record: check results, time, and cost (#lp-stateless).

### Scope cuts inside v0

- Board: all five columns and all actions, no subset (#werk-board).
- Multichat: fork, split, shared memory, open, tabs, park, follow, asks, live (#werk-mc-scope).
- Build loop: plan, builder loop, merge loop with the held-out set, overseer, stateless passes, pipeline tests, at full scope. The risk tier is fixed at feature (#werk-loop-tier).
- Trend reports are not built. The review still records MEDIUM and LOW findings per ticket, so a later trend report has its input (#werk-loop, #lp-prod-review).

## Testing Decisions

### What makes a good test

A test checks what a person or an agent sees from outside: a page in a browser, the exit code and output of a command, the events in the log, the branch and its commits, the board state. It does not check internal function calls (#st-build-seam). A visual test asserts on structure, and its screenshot is kept as evidence, not as the verdict (#werk-test).

### The seams

v0 is tested at two seams (#werk-v0-seams). Both are the highest seam for their half of the product, and both put one scripted fake agent binary first on the PATH, so no test reaches a real agent.

1. **The command line**, run against a temporary project directory and a temporary git repository (#st-build-seam). It covers every write path: the log events of each map verb, the ghost and accept rules, the contract check, reopen reasons and marks, excerpts, notes, and the whole build pipeline: plan, builder loop, merge loop, held-out set, and overseer. Every time limit is set to milliseconds.
2. **The browser**, through the Playwright test runner against a real server on a copy of a fixture project (#werk-test). It covers the map, card rendering and links, ghosts and the ✓, the chat pane, multichat tabs, park and follow, ask and death signals, and the board with its drawer and actions.

No seam sits below these two for behaviour. Pure code — the fold, the link rule, the Markdown renderer, the board fold — also gets unit tests and a 90% coverage gate over an explicit list of pure files (#werk-test). An I/O module gets a sampled list of named behaviours as its test cases, not a percentage (#werk-test).

### Runner and commands

`bun test` runs the server code and the React components. `bun run test:coverage` runs the same tests with coverage and then the 90% gate. `bun run e2e` runs the browser tests against the real server (#werk-test).

### Prior art in the prototype

- The prototype's browser specs boot the real server on a copy of a fixture project with a fake `claude` first on the PATH. They block the chat route and outside script hosts, clear local storage, and save a screenshot per test as evidence. The board specs run in order on one server, and the specs that write run last.
- The prototype has one fake Claude binary that replays a scripted event stream, and a test harness that makes a temporary project. The build tests use the same fake for the grader, the reviewers, and the classifiers.
- The prototype has a coverage-gate script that reads the pure-file list after the coverage run.

## Out of Scope

- The product diagram, the 3D graph, and the Flow view (#werk).
- The tracker export to Linear or GitHub Issues (#werk).
- The validate stage against production, and pipeline self-measurement (#werk).
- Trend reports across tickets (#werk-loop, #lp-trend).
- A spoken tier, tier escalation, and any tier other than feature (#werk-loop-tier).
- Any port of prototype code (#werk-base).
- Batch accept of ghosts (#werk-propose-new).
- Direct edit of a ticket on the board (#werk-board-control).
- A push of "what changed since your fork" into a tab (#werk-mc-shared).

## Further Notes

- #werk-mc-live leaves one point open: a dead background child pushes a line into the focused pane, while a pending ask only blinks. #werk-mc-asks sets red over yellow on every surface. v0 builds both signals for a dead child, the red dot and the pane line, because the card decides the line and rejects a silent dot.
- The overseer's 60-second silence and 5-minute loop check are tested only with parameterised limits and the fake agent (#werk-loop, #st-build-seam).
- The from-scratch build is itself the test of #werk-base: if the decided cards are not enough to rebuild a behaviour, the gap is a missing card, and the right fix is a new card, not a copy of prototype code.

58	45. As a person, I want several conversations at the same time, each in a tab, so that a second topic does not wait for the first (#werk-multichat).
59	46. As a person, I want a new conversation to fork the parent session, so that it shares the cached prefix and the understanding built so far (#werk-mc-fork).

61	48. As a person, I want each conversation to have a home card that names the tab and seeds the first turn, without a fence, so that a conversation can still go anywhere (#werk-mc-split).
62	49. As an agent, I want to read what a sibling conversation said from its session log on demand, so that I am not fed a diff on every tab switch (#werk-mc-shared).
63	50. As an agent, I want to read a card from the map before I write it, so that a stale context in my tab is never a wrong write (#werk-mc-shared).
64	51. As a person, I want a plain click on a card to move the map and keep the current conversation, so that I can browse while a turn runs (#werk-mc-open).
65	52. As a person, I want Shift+click on a card to fork a conversation rooted there and focus it, so that one gesture starts a new topic at that card (#werk-mc-open).
66	53. As a person, I want Shift+click on a card that already has a tab to switch to that tab, so that I do not fork the same card twice (#werk-mc-open).
67	54. As a person, I want a '+' at the end of the tab strip to fork at the open card, so that I can fork without a card link (#werk-mc-open).
68	55. As a person, I want the tab strip as the last row of the pane, with real tabs flush to the pane edges, so that the strip costs one row and never moves (#werk-mc-tabs).
69	56. As a person, I want each chip to show the home card id and a state dot, so that I can read every tab at a glance (#werk-mc-tabs).
70	57. As a person, I want Cmd+1 to Cmd+5 and Cmd+[ / Cmd+] to switch tabs, so that I can move between conversations from the keyboard (#werk-mc-tabs).
71	58. As a person, I want at most five visible chips, with the least recently touched idle tab parked, so that the strip stays readable (#werk-mc-park).
72	59. As a person, I want a running tab never parked, so that a live turn stays in view (#werk-mc-park).
73	60. As a person, I want a '…' menu that lists every conversation, marks visible, parked, and active ones, and shows the total count, so that I reach every conversation in one place (#werk-mc-park).
74	61. As a person, I want an un-park to resume the session from disk, so that a parked conversation continues where it stopped (#werk-mc-park).
75	62. As a person, I want a close control on a tab to park it at once, not end the session, so that nothing is ever closed for good (#werk-mc-park).
76	63. As a person, I want a parked session's process killed after 30 minutes idle, and resumed when I reopen it, so that idle processes do not pile up (#werk-mc-park).
77	64. As a person, I want focusing a tab to move the map to that tab's card, so that the map and the conversation always share one subject (#werk-mc-follow).
78	65. As a person, I want each tab to keep its own map position, so that switching away and back restores where I was (#werk-mc-follow).
79	66. As a person, I want an unsent draft to belong to its tab, so that what I typed under one card survives a switch (#werk-mc-follow).
80	67. As a person, I want a permission ask answered only on its own tab, so that a question never interrupts the tab I am reading (#werk-mc-asks).
81	68. As a person, I want a tab with a pending ask to blink, and the '…' button to blink when that tab is hidden, so that I see from any tab that another one is blocked (#werk-mc-asks, #werk-mc-live).
82	69. As a person, I want red to win over yellow on every surface, so that a dead child is never hidden by an ask (#werk-mc-asks).
83	70. As a person, I want a running dot on the chip and on the tab's home card in the tree, so that I see which turns still run (#werk-mc-live).
84	71. As a person, I want a tab with a background agent still going to read as running, so that a finished main turn does not look idle too early (#werk-mc-live).
85	72. As a person, I want a dead child in a background tab to show a line in the pane I am looking at, with the tab's name, so that I do not find a death by chance (#werk-mc-live).
86	
87	### The board
88	
89	73. As a person, I want a board with the columns blocked, ready, building, merging, and done, so that I watch the build as it runs (#werk-board-columns).
90	74. As a person, I want a ticket card to show only its title, a retry count after more than one retry, and a count of unmet blocking tickets, so that the board stays readable (#vi-board).
91	75. As a person, I want a building ticket with a live session to pulse, and stop pulsing the moment the session ends, so that the pulse means "a session runs now" (#vi-board).
92	76. As a person, I want a click on a ticket to open a drawer with the slice on the left and the metadata on the right, so that I can read a long brief and its relations together (#vi-board).
93	77. As a person, I want a click on a cited card id in the drawer to open that card on the map, so that I can check a ticket against its decisions (#vi-board).
94	78. As a person, I want a live log preview in the drawer of a building ticket, dropped when the ticket leaves building, so that I see the running session and not a stale transcript (#vi-board).
95	79. As a person, I want a red held-out step shown as a badge on the done ticket whose merge it followed, linked to the follow-up ticket, so that a known break is visible without a new column (#werk-board-columns).
96	80. As a person, I want to reorder tickets within ready, so that I choose the build order (#werk-board-control).
97	81. As a person, I want to archive a ready or blocked ticket after a confirmation that says it can be restored, so that I remove a ticket without losing it (#werk-board-control).
98	82. As a person, I want to trigger the build of one ready ticket inside an active run, by the trigger icon or by a drag into building, so that I start one ticket early (#werk-board-control).
99	83. As a person, I want to stop a building ticket by a drag back into ready, so that I can stop a build that goes the wrong way (#werk-board-control).
100	84. As a person, I want nothing to build before I start the run, so that the build order stays my choice (#werk-board-control).
101	85. As a person, I want every other column move made by an agent or by the merge loop, so that the board shows the real state of the loop (#werk-board-control).
102	86. As a person, I want to ask an agent to change a ticket, not edit it on the board, so that the ticket-set checks run again (#werk-board-control).
103	
104	### The inner build loop
105	
106	87. As a person, I want the plan to end with one spec per decided subtree, then tickets from that spec, so that all tickets split one agreed whole (#st-spec).
107	88. As a person, I want every answer that the spec or ticket writer gives and no card gives to come back as a proposed card, so that I can see and reopen every new decision (#st-spec).
108	89. As a builder, I want each ticket to be a tracer-bullet slice with what to build, acceptance criteria, stories, cites, blocked_by, and checks, so that one fresh context can build it (#st-ticket).
109	90. As a person, I want each ticket to list the spec stories it delivers, frozen at the build, so that done is stated from my side and fixed before the build (#st-ticket-stories).
110	91. As a person, I want blocked_by derived from the depends_on edges between the cited cards, so that the order is not a guess (#st-ticket).
111	92. As a builder, I want one ticket in one worktree, with a fresh agent per pass, so that a long context does not degrade my work (#st-build-ticket, #lp-stateless).
112	93. As a builder, I want the last failure, cut to about 4,000 characters, in the next pass's prompt, so that I know what to fix (#lp-stateless).
113	94. As a person, I want each pass committed, and one line per pass with check results, time, and cost, so that I can read what each pass did (#lp-stateless).
114	95. As a person, I want a check to be one command and its exit code, so that a check is never argued with (#lp-checks).
115	96. As a person, I want a grader to judge the diff against each decided card in the ticket's depends_on closure, with a score and the gap, so that a diff that builds the wrong thing fails (#lp-prod-judge).
116	97. As a person, I want five reviewers, one per quality area, to read the diff, so that problems no card names are caught (#lp-prod-review).
117	98. As a person, I want a CRITICAL or HIGH finding to fail the pass, and MEDIUM and LOW to be recorded only, so that the loop stops on real problems only (#lp-prod-review).
118	99. As a person, I want a retry cap, default 5, to stop a builder loop that does not converge, so that a run cannot loop forever (#st-build-ticket).
119	100. As a person, I want the merge loop to merge one ticket at a time after the checks pass on the run's tree plus the ticket, so that tickets that are green alone are also green together (#st-build-run).
120	101. As a person, I want a red check in merging to send the ticket back to the builder loop with the failure, so that a broken merge never lands (#st-build-run).
121	102. As a person, I want the held-out set to run after each merge, and a red step to file a follow-up ticket while the merge stands, so that a break is found at the merge that caused it (#st-validate-heldout, #st-g2-heldout).
122	103. As a person, I want the builder never to see the held-out steps, so that the builder cannot game the bar (#lp-prod-heldout).
123	104. As a person, I want G2 to wait until every held-out step is green on the final tree, so that I never approve a known break (#st-g2-heldout).
124	105. As a person, I want an overseer to act on an unanswered permission ask, an unintentional loop, and a tool call with no timeout, so that no agent stays stuck (#lp-overseer).
125	106. As a person, I want every run to be a feature run, with a tier event written at the start, so that every gate waits for me and every run has a first event (#werk-loop-tier, #st-tier-default).
126	
127	### The dev loop and the harness
128	
129	107. As an agent that edits werk, I want a change to the server code to reload the changed module in the same process, so that a live chat session survives my edit (#werk-hmr, #werk-dev).
130	108. As a person, I want a second server start on the same project to wait up to 5 seconds for the lock and then refuse, so that two servers never share one log (#werk-dev).
131	109. As a person, I want a client change to reach the page without losing my composer draft, so that a reload costs nothing (#werk-dev).
132	110. As an agent, I want to run the unit tests, the coverage gate, and the browser tests from the command line, so that I can see the result of what I build (#werk-test).
133	
134	## Implementation Decisions
135	
136	### Project base
137	
138	- v0 starts in a new, empty repository. Nothing is ported. The decided cards that #werk depends on are the spec. The prototype is a reference to read, not to copy (#werk-base).
139	- The kill criterion for the from-scratch choice is recorded on #werk. The prototype's behaviour sets the bar. If the criterion fires, the fallback is to extend the prototype code (#werk-base).
140	- Three parts: the log, the fold, and the web view (#werk). werk's log is its own working implementation of #pr-log, not a consumer of a separate engine.
141	- Bun runs the server TypeScript directly under `bun --hot` in dev (#werk-hmr). The client is React, transformed by Vite, so v0 has a client build step (#werk-stack). Islands are the hydration pattern, and progressive loading is a shape of the API, not a framework feature (#werk-stack).
142	
143	### Modules
144	
145	1. **Log.** An append-only file of events. Append and read only. No event is ever rewritten or deleted (#pr-log). A proposed card is its own event type, not a flag on an added card (#werk-propose-new).
146	2. **Fold.** A pure function from the event list to the map state: nodes with their latest words and status, live edges, held ghost edges, rollups, stale and paused marks with their trace, and the unchallenged count. A ghost sits in the nodes with a proposed flag and outside every derivation. Its edges wait in a separate set and go live when both ends are real (#werk-propose-new). Stale marks the next hop; paused marks every downstream card; stale wins over paused (#pr-wf-paused).
147	3. **Command line.** The only write path (#werk-write). Each verb appends events. It holds the contract check at the move to decided (#werk-contract), the accept gate for ghosts with its actor claim (#werk-propose-new), the find and remove verbs (#werk), the quote verb for excerpts (#werk-excerpt), the note verbs (#werk-chat), and the build verbs (#werk-loop). The command form of each verb lives on its own card under #werk-cli.
148	4. **Server.** One process per project directory, guarded by a lock with a 5-second wait and a port retry of 20 tries at 250 ms (#werk-dev). A guard on the global object keeps a hot reload from starting a second server or a second agent (#werk-hmr). It serves the client, the read API, and one live event channel (SSE). The channel pushes "changed" when the log changes and "reload" when the client code changes (#werk-dev). In dev, the server runs Vite inside its own process to transform the client. A client change that Vite cannot apply in place sends the "reload" event, and the composer draft is kept in session storage across it (#werk-client-reload).
149	5. **Conversation manager.** One Claude Code child per conversation, spoken to over stream-json (#werk-chat). It forks a session with the fork-session option (#werk-mc-fork), stores the session id and the home card of each conversation (#werk-mc-split), parks, un-parks, and reaps idle children after 30 minutes (#werk-mc-park), and keeps one ask at a time per conversation (#werk-mc-asks). It reports running, waiting, and dead per conversation (#werk-mc-live).
150	6. **Board state.** Ticket state is its own append-only log beside the decision log (#vi-board-state). The board view folds it into the five columns (#werk-board-columns). The board actions write to it through the server (#werk-board-control).
151	7. **Build pipeline.** Plan (spec, then tickets), builder loop, merge loop, held-out set, and overseer (#werk-loop). Each pass is a fresh headless agent in a worktree (#lp-stateless). Every time limit is a parameter (#st-build-seam). Every run writes a feature tier event first (#werk-loop-tier).
152	8. **Client.** Three views: the map, the board, and the chat pane (#werk). The Markdown renderer adds card links by the rules of #werk-reflink and boxes fenced code with highlighting (#werk-codeblock). The open card lives in the location hash. Each tab owns its card, its map position, and its draft (#werk-mc-follow).
153	9. **Fake agent.** One scripted binary that stands in for every Claude Code child: the chat agent, the builder, the grader, the reviewers, the classifiers, the step author, and the binder. It replays a scripted stream of events and edits files the way a real agent does (#st-build-seam, #werk-v0-seams).
154	
155	### Interfaces between the modules
156	
157	- The command line and the server both append through the log module. Neither writes a card in any other way (#werk-write).
158	- Every read goes through the fold. The browser, the command line, and the build pipeline read the same fold of the same log (#pr-log).
159	- The server talks to each agent over stream-json, as a child process (#werk-chat). The build pipeline starts a headless one-shot child per pass (#lp-stateless).
160	- The client gets the graph from the read API and refetches it on a "changed" event. It reloads itself on a "reload" event (#werk-dev).
161	- The board reads ticket state from its own log, not from card status (#vi-board-state).
162	
163	### Contracts
164	
165	- The chat request carries the text, the pasted images, the open card, and the active conversation tab. The reply streams over the live channel (#werk-chat).
166	- The server has a note route that appends a note and copies the `re #<id> "<title>": <text>` line to the clipboard. The browser never calls it (#werk-chat).
167	- An edge proposed with a card accepts or discards with that card, never alone. Accepting a child accepts its ghost refines ancestors. Discarding a card discards its ghost descendants. Accept is one card at a time (#werk-propose-new).
168	- A ticket has the fields title, what to build, acceptance criteria, stories, cites, blocked_by, and checks, and names no file paths (#st-ticket, #st-ticket-stories).
169	- The grader returns a score from 1 to 5, where 3 passes, and the gap for each card (#lp-prod-judge). A review finding has a severity, a file and a line, an impact, and a fix (#lp-prod-review).
170	- A builder pass appends one line to the run's record: check results, time, and cost (#lp-stateless).
171	
172	### Scope cuts inside v0
173	
174	- Board: all five columns and all actions, no subset (#werk-board).
175	- Multichat: fork, split, shared memory, open, tabs, park, follow, asks, live (#werk-mc-scope).
176	- Build loop: plan, builder loop, merge loop with the held-out set, overseer, stateless passes, pipeline tests, at full scope. The risk tier is fixed at feature (#werk-loop-tier).
177	- Trend reports are not built. The review still records MEDIUM and LOW findings per ticket, so a later trend report has its input (#werk-loop, #lp-prod-review).
178	
179	## Testing Decisions
180	
181	### What makes a good test
182	
183	A test checks what a person or an agent sees from outside: a page in a browser, the exit code and output of a command, the events in the log, the branch and its commits, the board state. It does not check internal function calls (#st-build-seam). A visual test asserts on structure, and its screenshot is kept as evidence, not as the verdict (#werk-test).
184	
185	### The seams
186	
187	v0 is tested at two seams (#werk-v0-seams). Both are the highest seam for their half of the product, and both put one scripted fake agent binary first on the PATH, so no test reaches a real agent.
188	
189	1. **The command line**, run against a temporary project directory and a temporary git repository (#st-build-seam). It covers every write path: the log events of each map verb, the ghost and accept rules, the contract check, reopen reasons and marks, excerpts, notes, and the whole build pipeline: plan, builder loop, merge loop, held-out set, and overseer. Every time limit is set to milliseconds.
190	2. **The browser**, through the Playwright test runner against a real server on a copy of a fixture project (#werk-test). It covers the map, card rendering and links, ghosts and the ✓, the chat pane, multichat tabs, park and follow, ask and death signals, and the board with its drawer and actions.
191	
192	No seam sits below these two for behaviour. Pure code — the fold, the link rule, the Markdown renderer, the board fold — also gets unit tests and a 90% coverage gate over an explicit list of pure files (#werk-test). An I/O module gets a sampled list of named behaviours as its test cases, not a percentage (#werk-test).
193	
194	### Runner and commands
195	
196	`bun test` runs the server code and the React components. `bun run test:coverage` runs the same tests with coverage and then the 90% gate. `bun run e2e` runs the browser tests against the real server (#werk-test).
197	
198	### Prior art in the prototype
199	
200	- The prototype's browser specs boot the real server on a copy of a fixture project with a fake `claude` first on the PATH. They block the chat route and outside script hosts, clear local storage, and save a screenshot per test as evidence. The board specs run in order on one server, and the specs that write run last.
201	- The prototype has one fake Claude binary that replays a scripted event stream, and a test harness that makes a temporary project. The build tests use the same fake for the grader, the reviewers, and the classifiers.
202	- The prototype has a coverage-gate script that reads the pure-file list after the coverage run.
203	
204	## Out of Scope
205	
206	- The product diagram, the 3D graph, and the Flow view (#werk).
207	- The tracker export to Linear or GitHub Issues (#werk).
208	- The validate stage against production, and pipeline self-measurement (#werk).
209	- Trend reports across tickets (#werk-loop, #lp-trend).
210	- A spoken tier, tier escalation, and any tier other than feature (#werk-loop-tier).
211	- Any port of prototype code (#werk-base).
212	- Batch accept of ghosts (#werk-propose-new).
213	- Direct edit of a ticket on the board (#werk-board-control).
214	- A push of "what changed since your fork" into a tab (#werk-mc-shared).
215	
216	## Further Notes
217	
218	- #werk-mc-live leaves one point open: a dead background child pushes a line into the focused pane, while a pending ask only blinks. #werk-mc-asks sets red over yellow on every surface. v0 builds both signals for a dead child, the red dot and the pane line, because the card decides the line and rejects a silent dot.
219	- The overseer's 60-second silence and 5-minute loop check are tested only with parameterised limits and the fake agent (#werk-loop, #st-build-seam).
220	- The from-scratch build is itself the test of #werk-base: if the decided cards are not enough to rebuild a behaviour, the gap is a missing card, and the right fix is a new card, not a copy of prototype code.

10. As a person, I want a ghost drawn grey or dashed under its proposed parent, so that I can tell "this card does not exist yet" from "this card has a pending change" (#werk-propose-new).
11. As a person, I want to accept one ghost at a time with a ✓ button, so that I read each card before it commits (#werk-propose-new).
12. As a person, I want an accept to also accept the ghost refines ancestors above the card, so that a click cannot orphan a card (#werk-propose-new).
13. As a person, I want a discard to also discard the ghost descendants of the card, so that no ghost hangs under a card that is gone (#werk-propose-new).
14. As a person, I want the words of a ghost frozen, so that what I accept is what I read (#werk-propose-new).
15. As an agent, I want link, status, and who to still work on a ghost, so that I can propose a card that is already decided, with its basis and options, as one unit (#werk-propose-new).
16. As a person, I want the edges of a ghost held, and live only when both ends are real, so that an accept needs no second event (#werk-propose-new).
17. As a person, I want a ghost outside every rollup, staleness mark, and unchallenged count, so that a proposal does not change the numbers before I accept it (#werk-propose-new).
18. As a person, I want an accept from the command line to refuse unless it states that I asked for it, so that an agent does not accept its own proposal by default (#werk-propose-new).

### The contract check

19. As a person, I want a card to move to decided only after a program check passes, so that the map's rules are not only prose (#werk-contract).
20. As an agent, I want a failed check to print the exact next command, so that I can fix the card in one step (#werk-contract).
21. As a person, I want the check to run on the held edges of a ghost too, so that a ghost proposed as decided obeys the same rule (#werk-propose-new, #werk-contract).
22. As a person, I want an amend of a decided card to run the same facts again, so that a change cannot skip the check (#werk-contract).

### Reopen reasons and staleness

23. As a person, I want a reopen to carry a reason, postponed or rejected, so that the marks on dependent cards say whether the content is still true (#pr-wf-paused).
24. As a person, I want a rejected reopen to mark the next hop only as stale, in red, so that each dependent card is reviewed in turn (#pr-wf-paused).
25. As a person, I want a postponed reopen to mark every downstream card as paused, in grey, with the status colour kept, so that deferred work reads calm and distinct (#pr-wf-paused).
26. As a person, I want stale to win when a postponement and an invalidation reach one card, so that a real invalidation never looks calm (#pr-wf-paused).
27. As a person, I want the staleness view to show the reopen reason of each mark, so that I know what to do with each card (#werk).

### Excerpts

## Implementation Decisions

### Project base

- v0 starts in a new, empty repository. Nothing is ported. The decided cards that #werk depends on are the spec. The prototype is a reference to read, not to copy (#werk-base).
- The kill criterion for the from-scratch choice is recorded on #werk. The prototype's behaviour sets the bar. If the criterion fires, the fallback is to extend the prototype code (#werk-base).
- Three parts: the log, the fold, and the web view (#werk). werk's log is its own working implementation of #pr-log, not a consumer of a separate engine.
- Bun runs the server TypeScript directly under `bun --hot` in dev (#werk-hmr). The client is React, transformed by Vite, so v0 has a client build step (#werk-stack). Islands are the hydration pattern, and progressive loading is a shape of the API, not a framework feature (#werk-stack).

### Modules

1. **Log.** An append-only file of events. Append and read only. No event is ever rewritten or deleted (#pr-log). A proposed card is its own event type, not a flag on an added card (#werk-propose-new).
2. **Fold.** A pure function from the event list to the map state: nodes with their latest words and status, live edges, held ghost edges, rollups, stale and paused marks with their trace, and the unchallenged count. A ghost sits in the nodes with a proposed flag and outside every derivation. Its edges wait in a separate set and go live when both ends are real (#werk-propose-new). Stale marks the next hop; paused marks every downstream card; stale wins over paused (#pr-wf-paused).
3. **Command line.** The only write path (#werk-write). Each verb appends events. It holds the contract check at the move to decided (#werk-contract), the accept gate for ghosts with its actor claim (#werk-propose-new), the find and remove verbs (#werk), the quote verb for excerpts (#werk-excerpt), the note verbs (#werk-chat), and the build verbs (#werk-loop). The command form of each verb lives on its own card under #werk-cli.
4. **Server.** One process per project directory, guarded by a lock with a 5-second wait and a port retry of 20 tries at 250 ms (#werk-dev). A guard on the global object keeps a hot reload from starting a second server or a second agent (#werk-hmr). It serves the client, the read API, and one live event channel (SSE). The channel pushes "changed" when the log changes and "reload" when the client code changes (#werk-dev). In dev, the server runs Vite inside its own process to transform the client. A client change that Vite cannot apply in place sends the "reload" event, and the composer draft is kept in session storage across it (#werk-client-reload).
5. **Conversation manager.** One Claude Code child per conversation, spoken to over stream-json (#werk-chat). It forks a session with the fork-session option (#werk-mc-fork), stores the session id and the home card of each conversation (#werk-mc-split), parks, un-parks, and reaps idle children after 30 minutes (#werk-mc-park), and keeps one ask at a time per conversation (#werk-mc-asks). It reports running, waiting, and dead per conversation (#werk-mc-live).
6. **Board state.** Ticket state is its own append-only log beside the decision log (#vi-board-state). The board view folds it into the five columns (#werk-board-columns). The board actions write to it through the server (#werk-board-control).
7. **Build pipeline.** Plan (spec, then tickets), builder loop, merge loop, held-out set, and overseer (#werk-loop). Each pass is a fresh headless agent in a worktree (#lp-stateless). Every time limit is a parameter (#st-build-seam). Every run writes a feature tier event first (#werk-loop-tier).
8. **Client.** Three views: the map, the board, and the chat pane (#werk). The Markdown renderer adds card links by the rules of #werk-reflink and boxes fenced code with highlighting (#werk-codeblock). The open card lives in the location hash. Each tab owns its card, its map position, and its draft (#werk-mc-follow).
9. **Fake agent.** One scripted binary that stands in for every Claude Code child: the chat agent, the builder, the grader, the reviewers, the classifiers, the step author, and the binder. It replays a scripted stream of events and edits files the way a real agent does (#st-build-seam, #werk-v0-seams).

### Interfaces between the modules

- The command line and the server both append through the log module. Neither writes a card in any other way (#werk-write).
- Every read goes through the fold. The browser, the command line, and the build pipeline read the same fold of the same log (#pr-log).
- The server talks to each agent over stream-json, as a child process (#werk-chat). The build pipeline starts a headless one-shot child per pass (#lp-stateless).
- The client gets the graph from the read API and refetches it on a "changed" event. It reloads itself on a "reload" event (#werk-dev).
- The board reads ticket state from its own log, not from card status (#vi-board-state).

### Contracts

- The chat request carries the text, the pasted images, the open card, and the active conversation tab. The reply streams over the live channel (#werk-chat).
- The server has a note route that appends a note and copies the `re #<id> "<title>": <text>` line to the clipboard. The browser never calls it (#werk-chat).
- An edge proposed with a card accepts or discards with that card, never alone. Accepting a child accepts its ghost refines ancestors. Discarding a card discards its ghost descendants. Accept is one card at a time (#werk-propose-new).
- A ticket has the fields title, what to build, acceptance criteria, stories, cites, blocked_by, and checks, and names no file paths (#st-ticket, #st-ticket-stories).
- The grader returns a score from 1 to 5, where 3 passes, and the gap for each card (#lp-prod-judge). A review finding has a severity, a file and a line, an impact, and a fix (#lp-prod-review).
- A builder pass appends one line to the run's record: check results, time, and cost (#lp-stateless).

### Scope cuts inside v0

- Board: all five columns and all actions, no subset (#werk-board).
- Multichat: fork, split, shared memory, open, tabs, park, follow, asks, live (#werk-mc-scope).
- Build loop: plan, builder loop, merge loop with the held-out set, overseer, stateless passes, pipeline tests, at full scope. The risk tier is fixed at feature (#werk-loop-tier).
- Trend reports are not built. The review still records MEDIUM and LOW findings per ticket, so a later trend report has its input (#werk-loop, #lp-prod-review).

## Testing Decisions

### What makes a good test

A test checks what a person or an agent sees from outside: a page in a browser, the exit code and output of a command, the events in the log, the branch and its commits, the board state. It does not check internal function calls (#st-build-seam). A visual test asserts on structure, and its screenshot is kept as evidence, not as the verdict (#werk-test).

### The seams

v0 is tested at two seams (#werk-v0-seams). Both are the highest seam for their half of the product, and both put one scripted fake agent binary first on the PATH, so no test reaches a real agent.

1. **The command line**, run against a temporary project directory and a temporary git repository (#st-build-seam). It covers every write path: the log events of each map verb, the ghost and accept rules, the contract check, reopen reasons and marks, excerpts, notes, and the whole build pipeline: plan, builder loop, merge loop, held-out set, and overseer. Every time limit is set to milliseconds.
2. **The browser**, through the Playwright test runner against a real server on a copy of a fixture project (#werk-test). It covers the map, card rendering and links, ghosts and the ✓, the chat pane, multichat tabs, park and follow, ask and death signals, and the board with its drawer and actions.

No seam sits below these two for behaviour. Pure code — the fold, the link rule, the Markdown renderer, the board fold — also gets unit tests and a 90% coverage gate over an explicit list of pure files (#werk-test). An I/O module gets a sampled list of named behaviours as its test cases, not a percentage (#werk-test).

### Runner and commands

`bun test` runs the server code and the React components. `bun run test:coverage` runs the same tests with coverage and then the 90% gate. `bun run e2e` runs the browser tests against the real server (#werk-test).

### Prior art in the prototype

- The prototype's browser specs boot the real server on a copy of a fixture project with a fake `claude` first on the PATH. They block the chat route and outside script hosts, clear local storage, and save a screenshot per test as evidence. The board specs run in order on one server, and the specs that write run last.
- The prototype has one fake Claude binary that replays a scripted event stream, and a test harness that makes a temporary project. The build tests use the same fake for the grader, the reviewers, and the classifiers.
- The prototype has a coverage-gate script that reads the pure-file list after the coverage run.

## Out of Scope

- The product diagram, the 3D graph, and the Flow view (#werk).
- The tracker export to Linear or GitHub Issues (#werk).
- The validate stage against production, and pipeline self-measurement (#werk).
- Trend reports across tickets (#werk-loop, #lp-trend).
- A spoken tier, tier escalation, and any tier other than feature (#werk-loop-tier).
- Any port of prototype code (#werk-base).
- Batch accept of ghosts (#werk-propose-new).
- Direct edit of a ticket on the board (#werk-board-control).
- A push of "what changed since your fork" into a tab (#werk-mc-shared).

## Further Notes

- #werk-mc-live leaves one point open: a dead background child pushes a line into the focused pane, while a pending ask only blinks. #werk-mc-asks sets red over yellow on every surface. v0 builds both signals for a dead child, the red dot and the pane line, because the card decides the line and rejects a silent dot.
- The overseer's 60-second silence and 5-minute loop check are tested only with parameterised limits and the fake agent (#werk-loop, #st-build-seam).
- The from-scratch build is itself the test of #werk-base: if the decided cards are not enough to rebuild a behaviour, the gap is a missing card, and the right fix is a new card, not a copy of prototype code.

# Spec: werk v0

## Problem Statement

A person who builds software with Claude Code works in a chat transcript. The transcript only grows. The decisions that the conversation settles are buried in it, and nothing shows which decision rests on which other decision. When one decision changes, nothing marks the decisions that depend on it (#visual).

The person also cannot see the build. An agent that builds from the decisions works in a terminal. The person does not see which slice of work runs, which one failed, or why. A long build stops when one agent waits for a question that nobody answers.

werk has a working prototype of the answer. Its code was written to find the right shape, not to keep. It has shortcuts and is difficult to change. The person needs a clean v0, built only from the decided cards, in a new repository. The rebuild also tests whether the decided cards are enough to rebuild the behaviour (#werk-base, #werk-base-repo).

The person works on more than one project. werk must work on any project, not only on its own repository, and a user must install it without first installing a runtime (#werk-projects, #werk-dist).

## Solution

werk v0 is a visual layer over Claude Code with three views: the map, the board, and the chat (#werk).

1. **The map** draws the fold of an append-only log of decisions (#pr-log, #werk-write). Each card has a reason, typed links, options, sources and excerpts. A card that an agent adds is a ghost until the person accepts it (#werk-propose-new). A card cannot become decided until a program check passes (#werk-contract). A reopen marks the cards that depend on the reopened card, stale or paused by its reason (#pr-wf-paused).
2. **The chat** sits beside the map. A message goes to a live Claude Code child with the open card, and the agent writes what the talk settles into the map in the same turn. The reply streams in, and the map redraws while the person reads (#werk-chat).
3. **The board** shows the tickets of a build in five columns. The person starts a build of a decided subtree with one press, triggers one ticket early, reorders, and archives (#werk-board).

Behind the board, the inner build loop turns a decided subtree into merged, tested code with no person in the middle: a spec, then tickets, then a builder loop per ticket, then a merge loop with the held-out set, with an overseer that keeps every agent from getting stuck (#werk-loop). Every run is a feature run, so every gate waits for the person (#werk-loop-tier). Every step writes to one pipeline log (#werk-v0-pipeline-log).

One werk server holds many projects. A switcher in the header opens any of them, and each keeps its own map, conversation, agents and history (#werk-projects).

v0 is a new project in its own repository. Bun runs the server TypeScript directly and hot-reloads it without killing a live agent. Vite transforms a React client built from shadcn/ui components (#werk-stack, #werk-hmr, #werk-dev). Every change passes the production checks before it merges and again on a clean machine after (#werk-checks). A newcomer, person or agent, starts from the repository and the map alone (#werk-devex, #werk-cc). A release build makes one executable file per platform (#werk-dist).

## User Stories

### The log and the map

1. As a person, I want every change to the map to be one event at the end of a log, so that nothing I decided is ever lost (#pr-log).
2. As a person, I want the map to be the fold of the whole log, with the latest words and links of each card, so that I read the current state and not a history (#pr-log, #pr-log-snapshot).
3. As a person, I want no view to edit a drawn card in place, so that the log stays the only store (#werk-write).
4. As a person, I want a control in a view, such as accept or remove, to append an event, so that every view redraws from the same log (#werk-write).
5. As an agent, I want the command line to be my only write path to the map, so that I cannot change the map in a way the log does not record (#werk-write, #werk-cli).
6. As a person, I want a bad event in a committed log set aside and listed as a problem, so that one bad line never hides the whole map (#pr-log-refuse).
7. As an agent, I want a write that breaks a map rule refused with the rule it breaks, so that no new bad line enters the log (#pr-log-refuse).
8. As an agent, I want adding a card under a parent to be one event, so that the log shows one change where I made one (#pr-log-one-event).
9. As a person, I want every open view to read the whole map again when the log grows, so that every tab shows the same map (#werk-write-changed).
10. As a person, I want a page to fetch the whole map each time its live channel connects, so that a write made while the server was down still shows (#werk-write-watch-start).
11. As a person, I want to remove a card with its refines subtree, its options and its excerpts, and restore it later exactly as it was, so that cleanup is never final (#werk-remove, #werk-remove-restore-undo).
12. As a person, I want a removal to keep the card's links waiting and its id taken, so that a restore brings the map back as it was (#werk-write-remove-links).
13. As a person, I want the ✕ on a card with children to ask whether the children go too or move up, with the counts, so that I can remove a bad parent over good children (#vi-remove-btn, #vi-remove-btn-reparent).
14. As a person, I want a proposed removal drawn in red, so that its ✓ does not look like the accept of an edit (#werk-remove-red).
15. As an agent, I want a find operation that lists open and proto cards in a subtree, without paused, stale or postponed cards, so that I find work I can do now (#werk-find, #werk-find-scope).
16. As an agent, I want a search operation over the decided cards, so that I find a decision before I make it again (#werk-cli-search).
17. As an agent, I want every command to accept a card id with or without a leading hash sign, so that a copied reference works (#werk-cli-hash-id).

### Proposals

18. As a person, I want every card, option, source and excerpt that an agent adds to enter as a ghost, so that nothing enters the map without my accept (#werk-propose-new).
19. As a person, I want a ghost drawn dashed under its proposed parent with the badge "proposed", so that I tell "this card does not exist yet" from "this card has a pending change" (#werk-propose-new, #al-ghost-badge).
20. As a person, I want to accept one ghost at a time with a ✓ button, so that I read each card before it commits (#werk-propose-new, #al-diff-cli-btn).
21. As a person, I want an accept to take the ghost refines ancestors, options, sources and excerpts of the card with it, so that a click never orphans a card or leaves it without proof (#werk-propose-new, #werk-propose-new-carry).
22. As a person, I want a discard to drop the ghost descendants and the evidence that no other card cites, so that nothing unreachable stays behind (#werk-propose-new-carry).
23. As a person, I want the words of a ghost frozen, so that what I accept is what I read (#werk-propose-new).
24. As an agent, I want link, status and who to work on a ghost, so that I propose a card that is already decided, with its basis and options, as one unit (#werk-propose-new).
25. As a person, I want a corrected ghost to keep its thread of notes with a marker where the new words begin, so that I see why the words changed (#werk-propose-new-discard-thread).
26. As a person, I want an accept from the command line to refuse unless it states that I asked for it, so that an agent does not accept its own proposal by default (#werk-propose-new).
27. As a person, I want an edit to a card shown as one card with the changes marked inside it, so that I never compare a before and an after by eye (#al-diff, #al-diff-cli, #al-diff-render).
28. As a person, I want a proposal that leaves a block of the body unnamed refused, so that no text disappears without a mark (#al-diff-cli-cover).

### The contract check and reopen

29. As a person, I want a card to move to decided only after a program check of four facts passes, so that the map's rules are not only prose (#werk-contract, #werk-contract-facts).
30. As an agent, I want a refused decide to list every missing fact with the command that fixes each, so that I fix the card in one pass (#werk-contract-fix, #werk-contract-all-missing).
31. As a person, I want a waiver of a fact to need a written reason, so that a deliberate gap differs from a forgotten one (#werk-contract-waiver-reason).
32. As a person, I want a card with no decider to need an option, so that a bare card is refused once, not twice (#werk-contract-no-decider).
33. As a person, I want a change to a decided card to be an amend that cannot leave it missing a fact, so that a decided card stays valid (#map-frozen, #werk-contract-amend-scope).
34. As a person, I want a reopen to carry a reason, postponed, invalidated or rejected, so that the marks say whether the content is still true (#pr-wf-paused, #werk-cli-reopen).
35. As a person, I want a change to mark only the next hop as stale, and a postponement to mark every card downstream as paused, so that the marks follow how each kind of change spreads (#vi-prop, #pr-wf-paused-reach).
36. As a person, I want every mark to show its trace, with the reason and the path, so that I can judge it without a log query (#vi-prop-trace, #vi-prop-trace-reason, #vi-onview-stale).
37. As a person, I want a review of a stale card to end in a confirm or an amend, so that no mark is cleared unread (#rederive-reason, #vi-prop-amended).
38. As a person, I want a card on a stale basis to wait, not go stale, so that a new card is not marked for a change it already knew about (#map-wait, #vi-prop-bornstale).
39. As a person, I want a postponed card to carry a grey postponed tag and stripes, and to stop its own paused marks when it is decided again, so that waiting work reads calm and resumes cleanly (#pr-wf-postponed, #vi-onview-postponed, #pr-wf-paused-resume).
40. As a person, I want a depends_on link to need a reason and never point to an ancestor or a descendant, so that every link carries meaning (#vi-prop-linkwhy, #vi-prop-nolineage).

### Excerpts

41. As an agent, I want a quote operation that finds the text exactly once in a spoken message of a conversation and writes an excerpt, so that no quote is written from memory (#werk-excerpt, #werk-excerpt-once).
42. As a person, I want an excerpt to point at the conversation, the session, the message position, the span, the speaker and the time, and to keep its own words, so that I find the quote again and still read it on another machine (#werk-excerpt-pointer).
43. As a person, I want an excerpt's words never to change and an excerpt never to exist without the card it supports, so that every excerpt is a true copy (#werk-excerpt-event).

### Card rendering

44. As a person, I want each card to have one page: a hero box on top and the sub-cards as tiles below, so that every card reads the same way (#vi-onview, #vi-onview-hero, #vi-onview-subcards, #vi-onview-look).
45. As a person, I want the map to open on the page of the root card, so that the root is one more card page (#vi-onview-root).
46. As a person, I want a card page to show its options, evidence, excerpts and links with ids, titles and reasons, so that the card carries its own proof (#vi-detail, #vi-onview-links).
47. As a person, I want a `#card-id` in any text to be a link shown as `#id`, only when the map can open that card, so that every link lands somewhere (#werk-reflink, #werk-reflink-label, #werk-reflink-inview, #werk-reflink-guard).
48. As a person, I want fenced code boxed and highlighted by any common tag name, and plain when the tag is unknown, so that code reads well and never breaks a card (#werk-codeblock, #werk-codeblock-langs).
49. As a person, I want a backtick span in a title shown as code, so that a command reads as something I type (#vi-title-code).
50. As a person, I want the rollup of a subtree shown as a bar, a labelled count line and separate flag chips, so that I see how much is left and what is wrong (#rollup, #ro-axes, #vi-counts, #vi-counts-card).
51. As a person, I want each view at its own address, with breadcrumbs, view tabs, a search box and a counts strip in the header, so that I move around the map from anywhere (#vi-routes, #vi-crumbs, #vi-tabs, #vi-jump, #vi-counts-header).

### Card wording

52. As a reader of a card, I want its words to describe its subject at the level of the decision, with no session narration and no code names, so that the card is still true when I read it cold (#werk-wording).
53. As an agent, I want the wording rules in my system prompt in every project, so that I write cards the right way without a separate check (#werk-wording-check, #werk-agent-instructions).

### The chat

54. As a person, I want to send a message with the open card, and have the agent change the map in the same turn, so that the talk turns into decisions with no copy step (#werk-chat).
55. As a person, I want one continuous conversation per project, docked on the right, that keeps going while I move across the map, so that the thread is not split by card (#werk-onechat, #werk-pane).
56. As a person, I want the reply to stream into the pane with a status line, rendered as Markdown, and grouped tool calls, so that I see the turn as it runs (#werk-progress, #werk-tool-collapse, #werk-blockid).
57. As a person, I want each part of a reply to stay under the message that asked for it, with a waiting mark on a queued message, so that a second message never confuses the answers (#werk-chat-turn-id).
58. As a person, I want every turn to start with the card I am looking at, or a one-line reminder, so that the agent never answers about the wrong card (#werk-card-blind, #werk-chat-no-card-line).
59. As a person, I want only a request with the server token from a loopback host to start a turn or change state, so that no other site or machine runs code on my machine (#werk-serve-trust).
60. As a person, I want a permission ask answered in the pane, and a question from the agent shown as a form, so that the turn waits for me and nothing widens a permission silently (#werk-approve, #werk-approve-bar, #werk-mc-askqa, #werk-perm-native, #werk-perm-mode).
61. As a person, I want "Always allow" choices kept per conversation, so that a permission given in one place does not apply in another (#werk-mc-allow).
62. As a person, I want to paste a screenshot that uploads at once and shows as a chip with an image number, so that a bad image shows before I send (#werk-shots, #werk-shot-chip, #werk-chat-image-inline).
63. As a person, I want a slash-command menu and a card search on # in the composer, so that I see what I can type (#werk-chat-cmdmenu, #werk-hash-trigger).
